decision_required: Whether parameterless RLS predicates may be wrapped in (SELECT ...) across 275 policies to stop per-row evaluation, given the blast radius covers every read and write in the product
status: Resolved — Product Owner replied "do all three" on 2026-07-27 after being shown the diagnosis and the three-part remedy
required_by: Before any further work on /field or /planning read performance
safe_interim_rule: has_planning_capability(), has_any_role(), has_permission(), has_role(), the zero-argument ccr_/dash_ helpers and bare auth.uid() take no row-dependent argument, so Postgres evaluating them once per row was pure waste: 1874ms on a 1230-row scan plus a 1185-loop SubPlan, 5728ms total, against an 8s statement_timeout. Wrapping in (SELECT ...) makes each an InitPlan evaluated once; measured 5728ms -> 44.2ms. Equivalence was proven BEFORE applying by evaluating old IS DISTINCT FROM new over every row of every affected table as superuser (RLS bypassed, so full-table coverage) for three identities: 981 checks, 327 distinct clauses, 0 mismatches, 0 errors. Row-dependent calls is_assigned_inspector(visit_id), inspects_same_factory(visit_id) and can_read_semantic_audit_object(...) are deliberately NOT wrapped - hoisting them would change meaning. ALTER POLICY only, so no policy was added, dropped, renamed or re-scoped and command/roles/permissive are preserved. DDL was generated from pg_policies into an explicit migration file, never applied by DO-loop, because a generated loop cannot be reviewed by grep. Nothing guards the wrapped form today: a later migration can reintroduce a bare predicate and silently restore the per-row cost. See CC-RLS-INITPLAN-WRAP-20260727-001.
